rule.title: An improvement is capitalized: counted 0.00 on its row, depreciated by the software

when_missing.because: A repair or ordinary expense unless a preparer says it improved the property

citation.wording: Improvements. You must capitalize any expense you pay to improve your rental property. An expense is for an improvement if it results in a betterment to your property, restores your property, or adapts your property to a new or different use. Table 1-1 shows examples of many improvements.

rule.open_point: Two answers, as the CPA asks it (2026-10-03): Expense, or Depreciate. Depreciate counts the cost 0.00 on its row and leaves it to the tax software's depreciation, never in the expense totals — unless the de minimis safe harbor is elected and the cost is within its limit (cap-de-minimis-safe-harbor, which runs after this rule). The routine maintenance and small taxpayer safe harbors are still answered Expense by the preparer.
